summary: Fixed the object detector (and calibration) failing on a built/staged bundle with 'python.exe: can't open file ...\bin\apps\mymatasan\ai\yolo_worker.py: No such file or directory'. The detector's worker-script arg was a repo-root-relative path (./apps/mymatasan/ai/yolo_worker.py) passed raw to Python, which resolves it against the process working directory. From the `make build`/`make stage` bin/ bundle the working directory is bin/, so the path doubled to <bin>/apps/mymatasan/ai/... and the worker couldn't be opened; Python exited immediately and the persistent detector hit a dead stdin pipe (the calibration 500). The app now resolves vision.detector.args script paths to an absolute path against the app HomeDir (resolveDetectorScriptArgs), so the worker is found whether running from the repo root in dev (HomeDir=apps/mymatasan) or the staged bin/ bundle (HomeDir=exe dir, with ai/ staged alongside). Legacy repo-root-relative config values are recovered by basename in <HomeDir>/ai. The training script and base-model paths derive from the worker directory, so they follow automatically. Default config args changed to the HomeDir-relative 'ai/yolo_worker.py'.
compatibility: Backward compatible: existing configs with './apps/mymatasan/ai/yolo_worker.py' still resolve (basename fallback to <HomeDir>/ai). Absolute worker paths are used as-is. Only the mymatasan default config.json/config.dev.json 'args' value changed to 'ai/yolo_worker.py'. No API change.
